about.title: Menlo Park Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal collision happens on a corridor like El Camino Real, Willow Road, or Marsh Road, the people left behind are often navigating grief and paperwork at the same time. San Mateo County crash data shows Menlo Park saw over 200 injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, with traffic tending to bunch up on Wednesday mornings between 8 and 10 a.m. Even in a city where fatal outcomes are thankfully rare in the record, a single loss changes a family's future. California's wrongful death statute allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a claim, and other dependents may qualify in certain situations. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect families with an independent attorney who can review the circumstances, explain the filing deadline, and help pursue funeral costs, lost financial support, and the value of a loved one's guidance and companionship. There's no cost to reach out, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Menlo Park Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Can Be Confusing
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to other dependents in certain cases. An independent attorney can help sort out who qualifies before deadlines pass.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Death, Not Discovery
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death to file, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, like a city road authority, may be involved. Getting matched with an attorney early preserves options.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: California law recognizes recoverable losses like burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help document these losses accurately as part of a civil claim separate from any criminal proceeding.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim under certain conditions. An attorney can walk through your specific family situation.

items.question: Does a criminal case against the driver affect our civil claim?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal prosecution. Even if criminal charges are filed, reduced, or never pursued, families can still bring a civil claim for their losses. The two processes run independently.

items.question: Our loved one died near Willow Road, does that change anything?
items.answer: Location itself doesn't change the legal standard, but if a government-owned road or intersection contributed to the incident, the deadline to file can be much shorter than the standard two years. It's worth having an independent attorney review the specifics quickly given Menlo Park's mix of state and local roadways.
